marker: # unit_length is the Repeat size column of Table 1 and ref_repeats is the number of repeats that
# table gives for S. Enteritidis NCTC 13349, confirmed there by sequencing and identical to the
# number it reports for the sequenced isolate 07-2642. Seven of the nine are fractional because
# the array ends in a partial unit, so the alleles of those markers lie on a grid offset from the
# integers and a call on that grid is exact rather than INTERMEDIATE.
# ref_size is the product these primers give in the NCTC 13349 assembly GCA_000009505.1, that is
# strain P125109, by in silico PCR. Every primer matches that genome exactly, with no mismatch and
# no second product. At five loci the measured length equals the DNA sequence length Table 2 gives
# for the same strain. At four it does not:
#   SENTR2  518 measured, 519 published
#   SENTR3  493 measured, 494 published
#   SENTR4  119 measured, 120 published
#   SE-7    719 measured, 717 published
# The measured length is used, because it is the product the published primers actually give in
# the stated reference. No allele moves as a result: the largest of the four differences is a
# seventh of a repeat at SENTR4 and the rest are a fortieth or less, all far inside the allele
# tolerance, so a published fragment size still rounds to the same grid point either way.
# The second size in the Table 2 column, in parentheses, is what the ABI 310 analyser reported.
# It is an assay property, runs 0 to 26 bp short of the sequence length, and is not used here.
# label carries the name Table 1 gives in Boxrud et al. for the five loci that have one, and the
# locus name otherwise. SENTR2 has no Boxrud name but is locus STTR7 of Lindstedt et al.
# No repeat unit sequences are published, so patterns is N/A throughout: alleles are called from
# amplicon length and the tandem count is not a cross-check. SE-7 could not be counted in any case
# because its 61 bp unit is a conserved 29 bp part followed by a variable 32 bp part.
